content:
Ivy: Hey folks 44b I'm at King's Cross all day tomorrow 3ec3e2 — looking for a quick sandwich or something that will survive a train ride. Any favs around the station? Prefer places open early.

Tom: If you want speedy + reliable, 'Pret a Manger' in the concourse is the obvious one but there's a nicer spot called 'Gail's' on Pancras Road for pastries and decent sandwiches.

Rina: For something proper, try 'The Parcel Yard' inside the station 37d37f373 4cd it's like pub food but sandwiches are solid and they open early for commuters.

George: If you're feeling fancy and have time, 'Coal Office' (King's Cross Square) has great flatbreads but it's pricier and slower. Not ideal for train eats.

Ivy: Any GF or vegan quick options? Teammate might tag along.

Tom: Wagamama is nearby (granary options) but not great for take-away on a train. For vegan: 'LEON' has clearly labelled vegan wraps and they're quick.

Rina: There's a small kiosk called 'Feya' near Pancras that does gluten-free sandwiches — tiny menu but good for grab-and-go.

Ivy: Perfect. Can someone drop addresses so I can map it?

Tom: Quick list:
```
Pret a Manger 4cd: King's Cross concourse
Gail's Bakery 4cd: Pancras Rd, N1C 4AG
The Parcel Yard 4cd: King's Cross Station, Pancras Rd
LEON 4cd: King's Cross St Pancras Lower Level
Coal Office 4cd: King's Cross Square, N1C 4TB
Feya kiosk 4cd: Near Eurostar entrance, King's Cross
```

George: Tip: avoid the main concourse at 5pm 605 it's chaos. Try Pancras Rd side lanes if you want quieter seating.

Ivy: Thanks all! Will probably do Gail's or Parcel Yard. If anyone's around tomorrow ping me 60a

lunchbot: Poll created "Morning sandwich pick" Options: 1) Gail's 2) Parcel Yard 3) Pret. Vote with :one:/:two:/:three:.

Tom: Voted :one:.

Rina: :two: for me.

Ivy: :three: if rush is real.
